Precalculus | Quarter 2 | Unit 4: Trigonometry

Grade Versus Angle

A 20% grade is only 11.3°

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 11–12
Topic
Right Triangle Trigonometry
Standards
HSG-SRT.C.6, HSG-SRT.C.8, HSF-TF.A.2

Students use SOH-CAH-TOA to find sides and angles of right triangles, convert trail grades to angles with tan−1, and solve angle-of-elevation and depression problems.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Use sine, cosine and tangent to find missing sides of right triangles.
  • Use inverse trigonometric functions to find angles.
  • Convert between percent grade and angle.
  • Solve angle of elevation and depression problems.

3Essential question

Why is a 20% trail grade so much less than a 20° slope?

5MTB connection

Trail signs and builders use percent grade; physics and ramp design use angles. They’re linked by tangent: grade = tanθ. Because tanθ is close to θ (in radians) for small angles, gentle grades in percent look much bigger than the same slope in degrees.

Angles of elevation help a rider (or a builder) estimate the height of a drop or tree from a safe distance.

The mathOn the trail
tanθGrade as a decimal
tan−1Angle from a grade
Angle of elevationLooking up at a drop’s lip
sinθRise per metre of trail surface
